findings.title: Referer is interpolated into a script string (reflected XSS)
findings.body: The embed layout writes request.referer into a single-quoted JavaScript string with <%= %>. On Rails 3.2 and 4.0 that helper escapes &, <, >, and double quotes, but not single quotes, and it is not a JavaScript escape. ensure_embeddable only checks that URI(referer).host equals SiteSetting.embeddable_host, and Ruby's URI parser allows ' and () in the query. A parent URL such as http://eviltrout.com/?x=';alert(document.domain);// therefore passes the host check and is rendered as parent.postMessage(..., 'http://eviltrout.com/?x=';alert(document.domain);//'); which runs in the Discourse origin. This layout wraps both the loading and best responses, and a normal blog page that includes the embed script sends the full parent URL (including query string) as Referer. Any logged-in user who opens a crafted link on the embeddable host executes attacker script in the iframe and can perform forum actions as that user. Pass a fixed origin (Discourse base URL) or JSON-encode the target origin; do not HTML-interpolate a request header into script.

findings.title: Imported HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized (stored XSS)
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import appends an attribution link by interpolating the raw URL into HTML (href='#{url}' and the link text), then PostCreator stores that string with cook_method raw_html and skip_validations. Post#cook (post.rb:133) returns raw unchanged for raw_html, skipping the markdown sanitizer and plugin filters. The embed view prints it with raw post.cooked (best.html.erb:19), and the normal topic page also treats cooked as HTML, so the payload runs on the Discourse origin for every viewer. The URL is attacker-controlled: /embed/best only checks a spoofable Referer host, then the retrieve job accepts any http(s) URL whose host equals embeddable_host. A URL Ruby will parse, such as http://eviltrout.com/?q='onmouseover='alert(1), still returns the real page on most blogs (query string ignored) and, after Nokogiri::HTML.fragment.to_html, becomes an anchor with an event-handler attribute. absolutize_urls does not strip script, on* attributes, or javascript: URLs. The RSS path is worse: PollFeed does CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) and imports that with no allowlist at all, so a feed body of <script> becomes a live script tag. import_remote's readability tag list still keeps a[href] and img[src], so javascript: links survive. Escaping the footer URL is required but not sufficient; sanitize imported HTML before it is persisted as cooked, including on the update path.

findings.title: Success template has invalid Ruby (`end if`) and cannot render
findings.body: The header branch is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which is not valid Ruby. ERB compiles the template before running it, so every successful embed (topic already imported, TopicView assigned) raises a syntax/template error instead of showing comments. The loading template is valid, so the iframe sits on "Loading Discussion..." until retrieve finishes and then 500s. The matching closer must be `<% end %>`. spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb never enables render_views, so it still expects 200 and will not catch this.

findings.title: RSS poll crashes because item content is often nil
findings.body: poll_feed always does i.content.scrub and then CGI.unescapeHTML. SimpleRSS leaves content nil for ordinary RSS 2.0 items (body is description and/or content_encoded) and for Atom entries that only have a summary. nil.scrub raises NoMethodError. There is no per-item rescue, and the job sets sidekiq retry: false, so one such item aborts the rest of the feed and the same crash repeats every hour. String#scrub also does not exist before Ruby 2.1, so this line fails even when content is present on 1.9/2.0. Use description / content / content_encoded with a nil guard, rescue per item, and do not let one bad entry (nil body, nil/short title, URI error, rate limit) skip the remainder. open(feed_url) also has no timeout, so a hung feed blocks the scheduler indefinitely.

findings.title: Spoofable Referer is enough to fetch URLs and create topics
findings.body: best enqueues retrieve_topic for any embed_url when the Referer host matches embeddable_host. Referer is fully client-controlled, the route is an unauthenticated GET, and TopicRetriever only compares URI(embed_url).host to that setting (lib/topic_retriever.rb:15). It does not restrict scheme beyond what open accepts, port, path, or redirects. import_remote then calls open(url).read (topic_embed.rb:48). open-uri follows redirects to other hosts by default, so an open redirect on the embeddable host (or a 302 to link-local/metadata addresses) becomes server-side request forgery, including port probes such as http://embeddable-host:6379/. The 60s throttle key is per URL, so an attacker can enqueue a distinct job and create a distinct public topic for every query string that returns HTTP 200, all as embed_by_username, bypassing SpamRulesEnforcer because import passes skip_validations. There is no body size limit or timeout, so this is also a memory/job-queue DoS. Require a non-spoofable control (signed embed token), re-validate every redirect hop against an allowlist, cap response size, and rate-limit imports globally.

findings.title: import_remote uses Kernel#open without requiring open-uri
findings.body: import_remote fetches the article with open(url).read but never requires open-uri. Kernel#open only treats the argument as an HTTP URL after open-uri is loaded; otherwise it opens a local path and raises Errno::ENOENT, so no topic is created. poll_feed.rb requires open-uri at load time, and TopicRetriever calls PollFeed before fetch_http only when feed polling is enabled, so on-demand import accidentally depends on that file having been loaded in-process. The Disqus thor task calls import_remote without requiring open-uri either. The call also has no read timeout or byte limit, and a nil doc.content then crashes import via contents <<. Require open-uri (or use a dedicated HTTP client), set timeouts and a max size, and handle nil/failed fetches without raising.

findings.title: Every cache-miss embed runs a full synchronous feed import
findings.body: When feed polling is enabled, perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inline before the single-URL HTTP fetch. That downloads and imports every feed item on the retrieve job, even though feed_key is computed in PollFeed and never used (no conditional GET). If the feed is slow, invalid, or hits the nil-content crash, the exception aborts perform_retrieve and fetch_http never runs, so turning on feed polling breaks on-demand embeds whenever the feed errors. URL comparison is exact, so a feed link that differs by trailing slash, http/https, or tracking params will not satisfy the embed_url; the expensive poll still runs and fetch_http then creates a second topic for the same article. Fetch the one URL directly, and do not let a feed failure skip that fetch.

findings.title: Embed lookup is a raw string match and ignores deleted topics
findings.body: topic_id_for_embed plucks topic_id for an exact embed_url match and does not check that the topic or post still exists. http://host/post, http://host/post/, and the https or utm variants are different rows, so the iframe misses the feed-imported topic and import creates duplicates. After a moderator deletes the topic, the row still matches, EmbedController builds a TopicView for a missing topic instead of enqueueing retrieve, and the URL is stuck. On update (line 32), embed.post is nil once the post is trashed (Post includes Trashable), and PostRevisor.new(nil) raises. That exception is not rescued in PollFeed, so one deleted import stops the hourly feed. Normalize URLs before save/lookup, and treat a missing topic/post as "not embedded" (or destroy the embed row on delete).

findings.title: Protocol-relative and non-root-relative URLs are rewritten wrong
findings.body: absolutize_urls treats every href/src that start_with?('/') as a root-relative path and does href.sub(/^\/+/, ''), which strips every leading slash. A protocol-relative image or link such as //cdn.example.com/img.png, which is common in RSS, becomes http://original-host/cdn.example.com/img.png and breaks. Relative URLs that do not start with / (images/a.png, ../a.png) are left untouched, so the browser resolves them against the Discourse origin and they 404 in the topic and in the embed iframe. Only rewrite a single leading slash, leave // URLs as protocol-relative (or prefix the scheme only), and resolve other relative references against the article URL. The same logic is duplicated for img at line 70.

findings.title: embed_url is varchar(255) but article URLs are often longer
findings.body: embed_url is a Rails string column, so PostgreSQL stores it as varchar(255), with a unique index on that column. Real article URLs with query parameters routinely exceed 255 characters. TopicEmbed.create! then raises (string truncation / statement invalid), the import transaction rolls back, and the embed stays on the loading page forever because no row is written. Use a text column (and a unique index on text, which PostgreSQL allows) before this ships; a later migration cannot silently widen rows that already failed to insert.

findings.title: Concurrent imports race and enqueue jobs before commit
findings.body: import does a check-then-act (where embed_url is blank, then create) inside Topic.transaction. Two retrieve jobs or a poll overlapping a retrieve can both pass the blank check and both call PostCreator. The unique index makes the second TopicEmbed.create! raise, rolling back that savepoint, but PostCreator#create calls enqueue_jobs after its inner transaction returns and before the outer transaction commits. Those Sidekiq jobs are not transactional: they run against a post that is not committed yet or that the unique-violation rollback undoes. The RecordNotUnique exception is also unrescued, so a racing PollFeed aborts the remaining feed items. Rescue the unique violation, re-read the existing embed, and enqueue post-processing only after the outer transaction commits.

findings.title: Creates do not bypass rate limits that the Disqus importer disables
findings.body: import passes skip_validations, which only turns off post validations and, in PostCreator, SpamRulesEnforcer. It does not skip RateLimiter::OnCreateRecord on Post. The update path passes bypass_rate_limiter: true, and lib/tasks/disqus.thor calls RateLimiter.disable around the whole import, but PollFeed and TopicRetriever call TopicEmbed.import with the limiter still active. If the embed user is subject to create-topic/create-post limits, a feed larger than that allowance raises mid-loop. PollFeed does not rescue per item and sets retry: false, so the rest of the feed is dropped and the next hourly run fails the same way. Disable the rate limiter for embed/feed creation the same way the Disqus task does, or the hourly import cannot keep up with a normal feed.

findings.title: Login-required forums redirect the embed iframe to the login page
findings.body: EmbedController skips check_xhr and preload_json but not the application login_required filter (redirect_to_login_if_required). Comment embeds are loaded anonymously in a third-party iframe. When login_required is on, that request is redirected to the login page before ensure_embeddable runs. The login page is sent with the normal X-Frame-Options policy, so the iframe is blank rather than showing comments. Anonymous readers, which are the main audience for an embedded comment box, never see the discussion. Skip the login redirect for this action and keep the embeddable-host check as the access gate.

findings.title: Disqus import now requires a live URL and drops category and date
findings.body: The importer used to create the topic locally from the export (title, permalink body, thread created_at, and optional -c category) and then attach comments, so dead or private links still imported. It now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote, which HTTP-fetches t[:link] and parses it with Readability. A 404, timeout, or non-article page skips the entire thread (the comment loop is inside if post.present?). The -c/--category option was removed, and import does not accept category or created_at, so threads land in the default category with "now" as the topic timestamp instead of the Disqus thread date. import_remote also does not require open-uri (see topic_embed.rb). Keep a local fallback when the fetch fails, and pass category and created_at through to PostCreator.

findings.title: postMessage origin check is an inverted substring test
findings.body: postMessageReceived accepts the event when discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) is not -1, i.e. when the configured URL string contains the sender origin. That is the opposite of an origin allowlist and also ignores e.source, so it is not limited to this iframe. Any origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl is treated as trusted. If discourseUrl is http://forum.example.com:3000/, a page at http://forum.example.com (port 80) matches at index 0 and can set iframe.height. Compare parsed origins for equality and require e.source === iframe.contentWindow. The same file concatenates discourseUrl + "embed/best" with no slash normalization (line 7), so a discourseUrl without a trailing slash requests a non-existent host path and the embed 404s.

findings.title: Rails 3 lockfile was not updated for the new embed gems
findings.body: ruby-readability and simple-rss were added to the Gemfile and to Gemfile_rails4.lock only. RAILS3=1 still uses Gemfile.lock (see the dual-boot lockfile switch at the top of the Gemfile). bundle install --deployment on the Rails 3 path fails because the lockfile does not match the Gemfile, so feed polling and import_remote cannot be installed on that boot path. Update Gemfile.lock as well, or the gems are missing exactly where PollFeed and TopicEmbed require them.

findings.title: Specs never render embed views or parse a feed
findings.body: The success examples stub TopicView and do not enable render_views, then an after hook expects HTTP 200. They therefore never compile app/views/embed/best.html.erb, whose `end if` syntax error 500s every real success response. spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb only checks that execute sometimes calls poll_feed and never feeds an RSS document, so the nil i.content crash is untested. spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb asserts cooked == raw, which records the unsanitized raw_html behavior instead of asserting that script and event-handler markup is stripped. Add a render_views example and a fixture-based PollFeed/import test that includes a normal RSS item and a hostile HTML body.
